correctness.rationale: Exact fiber count proves K is planar Kakeya with claimed cardinality. Complete square and nontrivial additive character orthogonality give the full pointwise Fourier transform, including v=0. The quadratic Gauss identity G²=eta(−1)q yields the fourth-power sum at each v and separates field types; fourth orthogonality uses q²E(K) normalization. Exact independent ordered pair counts agree in 12 fields (ten prime and two quadratic extensions), and direct Fourier coefficient enumeration agrees in five small fields. Numerical tests are supporting evidence, not the basis of the general proof.

originality.rationale: Fraser, arXiv:2505.09464v1, Theorem 2.4 proves existence of a Fourier-decaying probability measure on any finite-field Kakeya set, but not the uniform-measure transform or fourth-moment arithmetic of an extremal parabolic configuration. Blokhuis--Mazzocca, arXiv:0911.4370v1 Example 2/Proposition 7, prove planar minimality and its geometric classification but not the transform/energy. Inspected published-finding corpus exact quartic-graph energy and prime-power-ring parabola extension are genuinely different objects/invariants. Repeated targeted searches found no direct equivalent; older Gaussian-period literature remains a real priority risk.

value.rationale: The exact additive quadruple count of a minimum-size planar Kakeya set is a natural global invariant of its Fourier spectrum; this computation additionally yields an explicit uniform Salem witness and reveals an arithmetic split by q modulo four and the quadratic character of two. The full transform and all-field fourth moment quantify phenomena beyond existing size geometry and nonconstructive choice of Fourier-decaying probability measures. The object and invariant have independent mathematical motivation, not an arbitrary cutoff.
